newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sanwa Bank shares seen attracting buying interest.
newsitem.headline: Sanwa Bank shares seen attracting buying interest.

text.p: Sanwa Bank Ltd, which will be included in the Nikkei 225 average index on September 24, should attract 13 to 14 million shares worth of buying interest, market sources said on Tuesday.

New Japan Securities Co Ltd said average demand from investment trusts for each of the 225 shares included in the Nikkei index was about 4.8 million shares and arbitrage-linked interest was valued at about 8.2 million.
However, New Japan officials added that some investors may have bought Sanwa shares in advance, knowing they would be included in the index soon.

"There was speculation that either Sanwa or Asahi Bank Ltd would be candidates for the index and both shares were sought after, so actual demand may not even hit 10 million shares," a trader at a foreign house said.
"Also the element of surprise is missing, so there may not be any sharp rises in the share price," he said.
New Japan officials said there were not enough bank shares in the 225 index and that Sanwa shares, which have high liquidity, were not a surprising choice for the index.
Nihon Keizai Shimbun Inc, which manages the index, said it chose Sanwa in order to achieve a sectoral balance and due to its high liquidity.
Sanwa will replace Honshu Paper Co Ltd, which will be delisted from the exchange when it merges with New Oji Paper Co Ltd.
